### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. fetal akinesia deformation sequence 3  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.715)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:26594)

**Proposed mechanism:** DOK7 (HGNC:26594) —DISRUPTS→ Muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase (MuSK) signaling (GO:0007215); Muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase (MuSK) signaling (GO:0007215) —DECREASES→ Neuromuscular junction formation (GO:0007477); Neuromuscular junction formation (GO:0007477) —DECREASES→ Muscle development (GO:0007517); Muscle development (GO:0007517) —LEADS_TO→ Fetal akinesia (HP:0001270); Muscle development (GO:0007517) —LEADS_TO→ Arthrogryposis (HP:0002652). Loss-of-function mutations in DOK7 disrupt MuSK signaling, leading to impaired neuromuscular junction formation and subsequent defective muscle development, manifesting as fetal akinesia and arthrogryposis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of individuals with pathogenic DOK7 variants who do not exhibit fetal akinesia or arthrogryposis, or vice versa, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, the presence of a common, highly penetrant pathogenic variant in DOK7 with a frequency > 1% in gnomAD would also challenge this proposed causal link. _(variant: Any pathogenic DOK7 variant with gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DOK7 in neuromuscular development could reveal therapeutic targets for both congenital myopathies and fetal akinesia syndromes, potentially involving strategies to enhance MuSK signaling or support muscle development.
